extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: An elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. MMStar benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.publisher: University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks (SEED, AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU) with an automated pipeline using eight powerful LLMs as candidate inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage. Samples that could be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs are excluded. Then 16 leading LVLMs are used to gauge the difficulty of the samples and split them to four levels. Finally, based on the difficulty of the rough-filtered samples, strict manual review and selection are applied to curate 1,500 high-quality multimodal evaluation samples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data collected from existing multi-modal benchmarks: SEED (63.5% of initial pool), AI2D (13.8%), ScienceQA (9.0%), MMBench (5.2%), MathVista (4.5%), and MMMU (4.5%). Initial pool contained 22,401 samples.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated pipeline was developed to preliminarily filter out samples that do not meet visual dependency and minimal data leakage criteria. Two closed-source LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro) and six open-source LLMs (Qwen-1.5-72B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B, Mixtral-8x7B, LLaMA2-70B) sizing 20B or larger served as inspectors. Open-source LLMs were applied with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy. Only samples with hit counts of two or fewer hits (around 75% of LLM inspectors fail to provide the correct answer) were retained. This reduced the sample pool from 22,401 to 11,607. All questions were converted into a multiple-choice format.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review to ensure: 1) each sample's answer should be based on the understanding of visual content; 2) selected samples should cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples should require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. To expedite manual selection, hit counts of all 16 LVLMs on coarsely filtered samples were tallied and split into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). After considering both diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels, 1,500 high-quality samples were manually curated from the coarsely filtered set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Samples were evaluated for difficulty levels based on hit counts from 16 LVLMs and categorized into four difficulty levels: easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11 hits), hard (4-7 hits), and tough (0-3 hits).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three experts conducted the manual review process.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLMs used as inspectors: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, Qwen-1.5-72B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B, Mixtral-8x7B, LLaMA2-70B. Sixteen LVLMs used for difficulty assessment including GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, and various open-source models.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM's and LVLM's training corpora.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies two primary biases in existing multi-modal benchmarks: 1) Visual content is unnecessary for many samples - answers can be directly inferred from questions and options, or from world knowledge embedded in LLMs. 2) Unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training - models can answer some visual-necessary questions without visual content, indicating memorization of samples within large-scale training data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited to 1,500 samples. The paper acknowledges that even with careful curation, some degree of data leakage may still exist. The benchmark focuses on multiple-choice format questions. The authors note that maintaining sample visual dependency and reducing data leakage is an ongoing challenge.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). The benchmark is designed to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capabilities across 6 core capabilities (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes. Usage guidelines emphasize that samples should only be answerable based on understanding visual content, with minimal data leakage and requiring advanced multi-modal capabilities.
